questions.stem: In an AC circuit, what is the term used to describe the effective resistance that takes into account the combined effect of resistance, inductive reactance, and capacitive reactance?
questions.solution: The term used to describe the effective resistance in an AC circuit is impedance. Impedance accounts for resistance, inductive reactance, and capacitive reactance. Resistance is the opposition to current flow in a DC circuit, reactance is the opposition to current flow due to inductance or capacitance, and inductance is a property of a circuit that opposes changes in current.

questions.stem: What is the term for the current that flows in a circuit with only an inductor or capacitor, but does not result in any power dissipation?
questions.solution: Wattless current is the term for the current that flows in a circuit with only an inductor or capacitor and does not result in power dissipation. This occurs because the energy is stored and released in the magnetic or electric field without being consumed. Resistive current involves power dissipation, while inductive and capacitive currents refer to the type of component, not the nature of the current itself.

hi.stem: एक परिपथ में जिसमें केवल प्रेरक या संधारित्र होता है, धारा के प्रवाह के लिए क्या शब्द प्रयोग किया जाता है जो किसी भी शक्ति हानि के कारण नहीं होता है?
hi.solution: शून्य शक्ति धारा उस धारा के लिए शब्द है जो केवल प्रेरक या संधारित्र वाले परिपथ में प्रवाहित होती है और शक्ति हानि के कारण नहीं होती है। यह तब होता है जब ऊर्जा चुंबकीय या विद्युत क्षेत्र में संचित और फिर छोड़ दी जाती है लेकिन इसे उपभोग नहीं किया जाता है। प्रतिरोधी धारा में शक्ति हानि होती है, जबकि प्रेरक और संधारित्र धारा घटक के प्रकार के बारे में होती है, न कि धारा की प्रकृति के बारे में।

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a transformer?
choices: To change the voltage level of an AC supply
questions.solution: The main purpose of a transformer is to change the voltage level of an AC supply. This is done using the principle of mutual induction. The option 'To store electrical energy' is incorrect as transformers do not store energy. The option 'To convert AC to DC' is incorrect as transformers cannot convert AC to DC. The option 'To measure current' is incorrect as transformers are not used for measuring current.

questions.stem: In an ideal transformer, the power input is equal to the power output. What is the reason for this?
choices: There is no resistance in the windings
questions.solution: In an ideal transformer, the power input is equal to the power output because there are no energy losses. This is one of the assumptions made for an ideal transformer. The option 'There is no resistance in the windings' is not the main reason. The option 'There is no flux leakage' is a contributing factor but not the main reason. The option 'There is no magnetic field' is incorrect as a magnetic field is essential for the operation of a transformer.

questions.stem: If the frequency of an AC source connected to a pure inductor is doubled, what happens to the inductive reactance?
questions.solution: Inductive reactance is directly proportional to the frequency, so when the frequency is doubled, the inductive reactance also doubles. The other options are incorrect because the reactance is not halved, nor does it remain the same or become zero, as reactance is a function of both inductance and frequency.

hi.stem: यदि एक शुद्ध प्रेरक से जुड़े एसी स्रोत की आवृत्ति दोगुनी कर दी जाए, तो प्रेरक प्रतिघात पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?
hi.solution: प्रेरक प्रतिघात आवृत्ति के सीधे समानुपाती होता है, अतः जब आवृत्ति दोगुनी कर दी जाती है, तो प्रेरक प्रतिघात भी दोगुना हो जाता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि प्रतिघात आधा नहीं होता, न ही यह समान रहता है या शून्य हो जाता है, क्योंकि प्रतिघात प्रेरकत्व और आवृत्ति दोनों का फलन होता है।

questions.stem: In an LCR series circuit, the current amplitude is given by i = v / Z. At resonance, the impedance Z is equal to R. If a circuit has a resistance of 2 Ω and a voltage of 10 V, what is the current amplitude at resonance?
questions.solution: At resonance, the impedance Z in an LCR circuit is equal to the resistance R. The current amplitude i is given by i = v / Z. Substituting R = 2 Ω and v = 10 V, we get i = 10 / 2 = 5 A. The correct answer is 5 A. The other options are incorrect because they either use R instead of v (2 A), assume no division (10 A), or double the result (20 A).

hi.stem: एक LCR श्रेणी परिपथ में, धारा आयाम i = v / Z द्वारा दिया जाता है। अनुनाद पर, प्रतिबाधा Z प्रतिरोध R के बराबर होती है। यदि एक परिपथ में 2 Ω प्रतिरोध और 10 V वोल्टेज है, तो अनुनाद पर धारा आयाम क्या है?
hi.solution: अनुनाद पर, LCR परिपथ में प्रतिबाधा Z प्रतिरोध R के बराबर होती है। धारा आयाम i, i = v / Z द्वारा दिया जाता है। R = 2 Ω और v = 10 V के मान रखने पर, हमें i = 10 / 2 = 5 A प्राप्त होता है। सही उत्तर 5 A है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि वे या तो R के स्थान पर v का उपयोग करते हैं (2 A), भाग के बिना मान लेते हैं (10 A), या परिणाम को दोगुना कर देते हैं (20 A)।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation accurately reflects the English original in meaning, structure, and terminology. All technical terms are correctly translated and match standard Hindi-medium physics terminology.

questions.stem: A transformer is used to step up the voltage from 220 V to 440 V. If the primary coil has 100 turns, how many turns must the secondary coil have?

The option '400' would step up the voltage more than required.

questions.stem: In a purely inductive AC circuit, how does the current relate to the voltage in terms of phase angle?

questions.solution: In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current lags the voltage by π/2 because the inductor resists changes in current, causing it to reach its peak after the voltage does. questions.solution: In an AC circuit, when the current leads the voltage by π/2, it indicates the presence of a capacitor. This is because capacitors store and release energy in an electric field, causing the current to lead the voltage. Resistors do not cause any phase shift, inductors cause the current to lag, and transformers are not components that directly affect the phase relationship between current and voltage.

questions.stem: In an AC circuit, if the current lags the voltage by a phase angle φ, what is the effect of connecting a capacitor in parallel on the power factor?
questions.solution: Connecting a capacitor in parallel in a circuit where current lags the voltage introduces a leading current, which reduces the phase difference and increases the power factor. The option 'Power factor decreases' is incorrect. The option 'Power factor remains the same' is incorrect. The option 'Power factor becomes zero' is incorrect.

questions.stem: A capacitor is connected to an AC source. If the frequency of the source is increased, what happens to the current in the circuit?
questions.solution: In an AC circuit, the current through a capacitor increases when the frequency increases because capacitive reactance decreases with frequency. This is due to the inverse relationship between reactance and frequency in capacitors. Lower reactance allows more current to flow. The other options are incorrect because they suggest the current would not change or decrease, which does not align with the behavior of capacitors in AC circuits.

questions.stem: In a purely capacitive AC circuit, the power supplied to the capacitor over a complete cycle is zero. Why is this the case?
choices: Because the capacitor stores energy and releases it back to the circuit
Because the capacitor does not consume energy
Because the capacitor blocks the flow of current
Because the capacitor is not connected to the circuit
questions.solution: The correct option is because the capacitor stores energy and releases it back to the circuit. This happens because during one half-cycle, the capacitor charges and stores energy, and during the other half-cycle, it discharges and returns the energy to the circuit, resulting in zero net power consumption over a full cycle. The other options are incorrect because capacitors do consume energy temporarily, they do allow current to flow, and they are typically connected to the circuit.
